methods.notes: Home Assistant / rikroe filter: the vendor service UUID in the advertisement (active scanning enabled). Preferred, because it does not depend on the name a rebadge advertises.
EUROprog 2's filter, exactly as the vendor app applies it. A unit whose advertised name differs (a rebadge, if it does) is invisible to it.

host_compatibility.basis: Home Assistant's core integration and rikroe's bleak library run on BlueZ, their author reports it working on a Sygonix HT100 BT, and im-0/cometblue drove a Comet Blue through gattlib on Linux. Not run by this project.
The vendor's EUROprog 2 and ET Blue apps use the platform GATT client with no special handling (static analysis). Not run by this project.

identification.notes: The name is EUROprog 2's exact-match filter (it applies no UUID or manufacturer-data filter). The advertised service UUID is what rikroe's library and Home Assistant's integration scan for, reported working on a Comet Blue and a Sygonix HT100 BT; it is the only signal likely to catch every rebadge. No manufacturer data is documented. Genius BLE100 probably advertises the same UUID; whether Progmatic Blue or Progtime Blue do is not recorded, so after connecting, confirm by the ee01-ee40 characteristics rather than the ef range (protocol_details.sibling_devices).

device.name: Eurotronic Comet Blue Bluetooth Radiator Thermostat (and Sygonix / Xavax / Silvercrest rebadges)
device.notes:
Battery-powered radiator thermostat (TRV) head sold in Europe by Eurotronic Technology GmbH and rebadged by Sygonix (HT100 BT), Xavax (Hama) and Lidl Silvercrest (RT2000BT). It drives the valve itself from an on-device weekly schedule; the phone only reads and writes settings. Transport is BLE GATT only, phone-direct: no bonding, no hub, no cloud. EUROprog 2's only HTTP traffic downloads firmware images, and ET Blue's only URLs are the vendor's help pages. If the vendor disappeared tomorrow, nothing a client needs would go with it.
ACCESS CONTROL is an app-layer PIN, not Bluetooth pairing: after connecting, a client writes the PIN (0-999999) to 47e9ee30-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67 as a uint32 little-endian. Every other write is refused until that write succeeds, and im-0's client reads none of the valve's own settings before it either. The manual's factory PIN "000 000" is the integer 0 on the wire (00 00 00 00). ET Blue makes the owner set a per-room PIN and refuses 0, so a unit set up with ET Blue no longer answers to 0. There is no framing, checksum or encryption anywhere, and the PIN travels in cleartext over an unencrypted link: anyone who sniffs one session learns it.
GATT: one vendor service, 47e9ee00-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67, every setting a fixed-length value on its own characteristic under the vendor base 47e9xxxx-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67 — clock (ee01), seven day schedules (ee10-ee16), eight holiday slots (ee20-ee27), flags (ee2a), the temperature block (ee2b), battery (ee2c), two little-understood values (ee2d, ee2e), the PIN (ee30) and the firmware-update channel (ee40); plus the standard Device Information strings. Temperatures are one byte of °C × 2 everywhere. In the temperature block and holiday slots, 0x80 means "leave this field as it is", so one field can be written without reading the others first.
SAME BASE, OTHER PRODUCTS: the same app family drives two unrelated siblings on the same UUID base — Progmatic Blue (a programming stick, 47e9ef01-47e9ef41) and Progtime Blue (a socket timer, 47e9ef51-47e9ef62, PIN at ef62). They are out of scope and listed in protocol_details.sibling_devices only so a client can tell them apart. ET Blue also drives a "Genius BLE100" with the same 47e9ee UUIDs, which probably shares this table (unverified). The Comet ZERO Blue is not in either app's device list and must not be assumed compatible.
DISCOVERY: EUROprog 2 matches the advertised name "Comet Blue" exactly and nothing else. Home Assistant and rikroe's library match the advertised service UUID 47e9ee00-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67 instead, which is the better filter: the rebadges' advertised names have not been recorded, and a name-only scanner may miss them.

openness.notes: Eurotronic has never published the GATT protocol. im-0/cometblue (2016) and rikroe's library (2020-2026, now behind Home Assistant's core eurotronic_cometblue integration) recovered it independently; the vendor app agrees with both field for field.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The valve accepts a connection and a PIN write whenever it is powered; there is no pairing button or window.

exclusivity.recovery: Close EUROprog 2, ET Blue or any other controller holding a connection before connecting. Nothing needs clearing afterwards: no bond is stored on either side.

pairing.notes: Link layer: nothing pairs and nothing bonds. The access control is the PIN write in `initialization`, which every connection must repeat. Nothing binds a client, so revoking one means changing the PIN (change_pin) — which every other client then has to be told.

pin.notes: The factory value, the same on every unit: the manual prints it as "000 000", Home Assistant as "000000", and on the wire it is the integer 0, written as 00 00 00 00. It is an application-layer PIN written to 47e9ee30-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67, never a Bluetooth passkey — no OS pairing dialog appears. Owners change it (0-999999, at most six digits) in EUROprog 2; ET Blue insists on a per-room PIN and rejects 0.

credentials.notes: The PIN is not issued to a client; the owner supplies it, and a client must store it and present it on every connection. It crosses the air in cleartext. There is no Wi-Fi.
stored_on_device: Weekly schedule, holiday slots, comfort/eco setpoints, offset, window-open settings, child lock

factory_reset.description: The menu reset is the manual's "All reset". Pulling the batteries for a few seconds is a different thing — the manual's remedy for an error code, a restart that keeps the schedule — and is not a factory reset.
factory_reset.effect: Per the manual, returns the valve to factory settings "ready for configuration as described for initial operation": schedules back to the default (one heating period, 07:00-22:00), comfort 21 °C, eco 16 °C. Whether it also restores PIN 0 is not stated in the manual and has not been established — which matters, because the menu reset is the only recovery for a forgotten PIN if it does.

procedures.basis: Eurotronic's English user manual (2015/06), section "All reset". Not performed by this project.
procedures.name: All reset from the valve's own menu

steps.action: Turn the selector wheel to the reset menu item and press OK.
When OK flashes, press OK again to confirm.
steps.expect: The valve restarts in factory settings and begins the initial-operation flow (date and time prompt).

ble.pin_source: App-layer PIN, not a link-layer passkey: factory default 0 (manual "000 000"); owners change it in EUROprog 2 or ET Blue.

methods.description: Scan for the vendor service UUID (or the name "Comet Blue"), connect, write the PIN to 47e9ee30-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67 as uint32 little-endian with a write-with-response, then read and write the setting characteristics. This is the vendor app's sequence, recovered by static analysis.

steps.action: Insert the batteries, set the date and time on the valve's own wheel when it asks, mount it at the INST prompt and let the adaptation run finish (manual, "Setting date and time" and "Adaptation").
steps.expect: The display returns to normal mode after adapting.

steps.action: Scan for advertised service 47e9ee00-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67, or for the exact local name "Comet Blue".
Connect and discover services. No bonding is requested or needed.
Optionally read the Device Information strings (firmware revision 00002a26-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, software revision 00002a28-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb); they are readable before the PIN.
Write the PIN to 47e9ee30-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67 as a uint32 little-endian, with a write request (not a write command), before anything else.
steps.expect: Write status 0 = accepted. Any other status is a wrong PIN (whether the valve answers with an ATT error or drops the link is not established).

steps.action: Write the current local date and time to 47e9ee01-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67, then read battery (47e9ee2c-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67) and the temperature block (47e9ee2b-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67).
steps.expect: Battery reads 0xFF until the valve has measured it; the vendor app re-reads after 1 s.

steps.action: Disconnect when finished. rikroe's library documents that the valve applies written settings when the connection closes, not at the moment of the write.
steps.expect: A fresh connection reads back the new values.

timing.notes: The vendor app compares the firmware revision string (00002a26-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb) against a fixed reference revision and, when the unit's sorts lower, waits 1 s after reading it before writing the PIN; on newer firmware it writes at once. A client that always waits 1 s covers both. The app serialises GATT operations: one outstanding read or write per device at a time.

causes: No PIN written yet in this connection — the valve refuses all writes until one succeeds.
Wrong PIN. A unit configured with ET Blue has a per-room PIN and no longer accepts 0; a second-hand unit carries its previous owner's PIN.
On older firmware the PIN went out too soon after connecting; wait 1 s and retry.
troubleshooting.symptom: Every write fails straight after connecting.

causes: The scanner matches only the exact name "Comet Blue" (EUROprog 2 does); a rebadge may advertise another name. Filter on service 47e9ee00-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67 instead.
troubleshooting.symptom: Found by Home Assistant but not by a name-filtered scanner.

causes: The client put 0x00 rather than 0x80 in the manual-setpoint byte (ee2b byte 1). rikroe's library does this when that field is not supplied, and its own climate entity works around it by always resending the setpoint. Send 0x80 in every field you are not changing.
troubleshooting.symptom: The valve goes to OFF after a third-party client changed only comfort or eco.

causes: rikroe's library documents that the valve applies writes when the link closes. Disconnect, reconnect and read again before concluding the write failed.
troubleshooting.symptom: A value written over BLE reads back unchanged in the same connection.

causes: In AUTO the valve returns to its schedule at the next switch point — by design (manual; Home Assistant documentation).
A holiday slot is in progress: the valve holds the holiday temperature. Home Assistant's documentation says to end it from the valve's MENU button.
troubleshooting.symptom: A setpoint written over BLE does not stick.

setup.notes:
Nothing is provisioned: the valve joins no network and holds no bond. A client scans, connects, writes the PIN (see `initialization`) and then reads and writes settings. Confidence is high because two working open implementations (im-0/cometblue, rikroe's library behind Home Assistant's core integration) do exactly this; this project has not replayed it.
Before any of that, the valve itself must be commissioned on its own buttons: after the first battery insertion it asks for the date and time on its display, drives the motor to its install position, and after mounting runs an adaptation to learn the valve stroke (manual, "Adaptation"). A unit that has not finished adapting still talks BLE but does not regulate.

rejoin.notes: There is no network membership and no bond. A new phone or controller needs only the current PIN. If nobody knows the PIN (a used unit, or one set up in ET Blue), the menu reset is the only recourse, and whether it clears the PIN is unknown.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project, and the research store holds no capture of this device. Every byte layout here comes from static analysis of the vendor apps (EUROprog 2 and ET Blue, 2026-09-27), cross-checked against im-0/cometblue and rikroe's library, whose authors ran them on hardware (a Comet Blue and a Sygonix HT100 BT). Per-fact verification is therefore `reported` throughout.

variants.notes: The original. Advertises the exact name "Comet Blue" (EUROprog 2's filter). Device Information reads manufacturer "eurotronic gmbh" and model "comet blue" when lower-cased, the pair im-0 identifies it by.

Rebadge; rikroe's library is developed on one and Home Assistant lists it. Its advertised name has not been recorded. im-0's README shows a unit whose software revision carries a Sygonix suffix and whose GAP device name is "Comet Blue", which suggests at least some advertise the same name.
Rebadge listed by Home Assistant and rikroe (untested there). Advertised name and exact model number not recorded.
Lidl rebadge listed by Home Assistant and rikroe (untested there). Advertised name not recorded.

entities.name: Radiator Thermostat
entities.notes: Target is the live setpoint (ee2b byte 1). In AUTO a new target lasts until the next schedule switch point. A target of 7.5 or 28.5 read back is the OFF / ON code, not a temperature — see the Valve Off and Valve Fully Open buttons. Requires the PIN write first.

entities.name: Valve Off
entities.notes: Setpoint OFF (code 15): closes the valve; the valve's own frost protection stays active (manual).

entities.name: Valve Fully Open
entities.notes: Setpoint ON (code 57): valve fully open until the next schedule switch point in AUTO.

entities.name: Comfort Temperature
entities.notes: The OFF (15) and ON (57) codes are valid here too but are left off this slider; send them through the command directly.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: 255 = not measured yet; re-read after a second.

entities.name: Child Lock
entities.notes: Read-only here: changing it is a read-modify-write of ee2a (the advanced write_flags command), which no single-role control can express safely.

entities.name: Manual Mode
entities.notes: On = MANU (no schedule), off = AUTO. rikroe's reading of ee2a byte 0 bit 0; switching it is write_flags.

evidence.app_static_analysis: EUROprog 2 (2026-09-27): the scanner's exact-name filter; the per-UUID write encoders and read parsers for ee01-ee40 and the two Device Information revision strings; the PIN gate that holds every other operation until ee30's write succeeds; the PIN entry limits (at most six digits, 0-999999); the pickers that bound every temperature, offset and window value; the child-lock bit; the battery parser's -1..99 window; the post-PIN connect sequence; and the firmware-update screen (header, block and status handling, download URLs). ET Blue (Flutter): only its string table was read — the two product names, the 47e9ee UUIDs, and the PIN rules (per-room PIN, 0 refused).

artifacts.description: Native Java, R8-obfuscated; decompiled. Source of the byte layouts, PIN gate, connect sequence and update flow. No cloud backend; its only HTTP use is the (now dead) firmware download.

Flutter; strings only (no Dart decompile). Established the Comet Blue / Genius BLE100 pairing, the shared 47e9ee UUIDs and the PIN rules. Negative finding: no firmware-update path and no network backend beyond help pages.

evidence.documentation_review: Eurotronic's English manual (2015/06): factory PIN "000 000", menu reset, factory temperatures and schedule, open-window options (10-60 min, three sensitivities), the child-lock button chord, and the six-profile vacation claim that the eight GATT slots contradict. The 2018 German manual's vendor URL is dead. No FCC filing exists; the product is EU-only.
evidence.open_questions: Everything under remaining_unknowns. The first things to settle on hardware are the real GATT table and properties (an nRF Connect dump) and what a wrong PIN looks like on the air.
evidence.open_source_cross_check: im-0/cometblue and rikroe's library agree with the app on every layout both cover, and add what the apps never do: the 0x80 unchanged filler, PIN-gated reads, ee2d/ee2e, the manual-setpoint write, the manual-mode bit, holiday-in-progress markers, advertised-service-UUID discovery, and (rikroe) that writes take effect when the link closes.

dfu_mode.notes: No update-mode name, address or service is recorded.

enter.notes: From the client's side there is no separate entry command: the app opens notifications on ee40 over the normal, PIN-authenticated connection and starts the transfer there. Whether the valve reboots into a loader at some point is not known.

image.notes: Two images, one for the radio module and one for the valve controller, which EUROprog 2 downloads from the vendor's website with a plain unauthenticated GET. Both URLs answered 404 on 2026-09-27 and no archived copy exists, so no image has been examined. The only integrity check the app applies is a CRC per block; the header carries no signature. The app's name for the radio image points to Dialog's SUOTA lineage and so, by inference only, a Dialog DA1458x radio; the protocol on ee40 is Eurotronic's own, not Dialog's SUOTA GATT service.

dfu.notes: App-derived only (EUROprog 2's update screen). The app offers an update only on units whose software revision is at or above a minimum, and updates the radio image before the controller image. ET Blue carries no update path. See protocol_details.firmware_update for the role-level flow; it is flagged advanced there.

recovery.notes: The valve's notification codes include "restart" (the app starts over from the header), which suggests an interrupted transfer can be retried, but nothing is known about what an interrupted flash leaves behind.

encoding_conventions.multi_byte: Only the PIN is wider than one byte: uint32 little-endian.
encoding_conventions.schedule_time: One byte, minutes since midnight / 10 (0-144); 0xFF = unused pair.
encoding_conventions.unchanged_filler: 0x80 in a temperature-block or holiday byte leaves that field as it is (im-0, rikroe). Not valid for the flags byte, where 0x80 is the child lock.

firmware_update.advanced_reason: Writes a new firmware image into the valve over ee40. The image is unsigned and checked only by a per-block CRC, the vendor's image downloads are gone, and nothing is known about recovery from an interrupted or malformed transfer: the likely outcome is a valve that no longer regulates and cannot be reflashed without the vendor. There is no recovery path to offer, so this spec deliberately stops at role level.
firmware_update.flow: Role level only. The transfer runs over ee40 on the normal, PIN-authenticated connection, with notifications open. It opens with one 20-byte header that names the image type and its length. The image follows in 20-byte blocks, each carrying a 16-bit block number, 16 image bytes and a CRC-16 over the block's first 18 bytes. The valve paces the transfer with notifications that carry a block number and a status code (status_codes). The vendor app sends the radio image before the controller image.
firmware_update.notes: Recorded so that an owner seeing these notifications knows what they are, and so a replacement client knows to leave ee40 alone. The header bytes, the image names and the upload sequence in full are deliberately not documented here.

status_codes.0x01: Block received: send the next one.
status_codes.0x02: Restart: the vendor app begins again with the header.
status_codes.0xaa: Header accepted: send the first block.
status_codes.0xbb: Busy: the vendor app waits 3 s and resends.

pin_gate.exempt_from_gate: The vendor app sends writes to ee30 (and Progtime Blue's ef62) and reads of the firmware and software revision strings (00002a26-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, 00002a28-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb) before authenticating; it queues everything else until the PIN write reports success. im-0 marks every vendor characteristic except ee30 as needing the PIN for reads too.
pin_gate.wrong_pin: The vendor app treats any non-zero write status on ee30 as a wrong PIN and prompts again. ET Blue has a dedicated "unknown PIN" state for a valve that refuses 0 and a separate refusal of 0 as a room PIN.

comet_zero_blue.notes: Not in EUROprog 2's or ET Blue's device lists. Do not assume it speaks this protocol.

genius_ble100.notes: ET Blue carries the same 47e9ee00 service and 47e9ee.. characteristic UUIDs for both products, so it probably shares this table. Not verified: ET Blue's Dart code was not decompiled, only its strings read.
genius_ble100.what: A second product ET Blue drives alongside Comet Blue; by its name another Eurotronic valve head, not examined.

sibling_devices.notes: Out of scope; listed only so a client that connects to the wrong product can tell. They share the UUID base and the EUROprog 2 app, and nothing else here applies to them.

progmatic_blue.what: Programming stick that loads schedules into Eurotronic valves through a wired port.

progtime_blue.notes: ef52-ef58 are 16-byte day programs, ef59 a flags byte, and ef62 its PIN (the counterpart of ee30).

test_vectors.notes: Constructed from the layouts above, not captured. The temperature read reproduces the decoded values im-0's README prints for its unit.
test_vectors.schedule_factory_default_07_00_to_22_00: 2a 84 ff ff ff ff ff ff
test_vectors.temperatures_read: 2e 20 20 2a 00 04 0a  (current 23.0 °C, setpoint 16.0, eco 16.0, comfort 21.0, offset 0.0, sensitivity 4 = high, 10 min)

uuid_base.notes: Every vendor UUID in this product family differs only in the four hex digits after "47e9". The vendor app sorts a characteristic into a product by those digits: below ee50 is Comet Blue, ee50-ef4f Progmatic Blue, ef50 and above Progtime Blue.

remaining_unknowns: The real GATT table: handles, characteristic properties (those here are inferred from use), whether the Device Information characteristics sit in a standard Device Information service (0000180a-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb), and whether ee40 needs the PIN for its notifications as well as its writes.
What a wrong PIN looks like: an ATT error on the write, a disconnect, or both — and whether repeated wrong PINs lock the valve out.
Whether the menu "All reset" restores PIN 0. It decides whether a second-hand unit with an unknown PIN is recoverable at all.
The flags block (ee2a) beyond byte 0 bit 7 (child lock, vendor app) and bit 0 (manual mode, rikroe only).

What the valve does with a temperature-block byte outside 15-57 that is not 0x80 — 0x00 for one, which rikroe's library writes into the setpoint byte by mistake and which a code comment in rikroe's Home Assistant component says turns the valve OFF.
The advertised names of the Sygonix HT100 BT, Xavax and Silvercrest RT2000BT rebadges (and whether every unit advertises the 47e9ee00 service UUID, or only some firmware).
Whether Genius BLE100 shares this table (likely: ET Blue uses the same 47e9ee UUIDs for it). The Comet Zero Blue is in neither app and must not be assumed compatible.

The meaning and unit of ee2e (im-0's "LCD timer") and the content of ee2d, and why im-0's example unit reports open-window sensitivity 4 when the manual calls medium (8 in the app's coding) the default.
Whether written values really take effect only when the link closes (rikroe's README says so) or at once, and whether that holds for every characteristic or only the temperature block.
Whether one central at a time is enforced (the vendor apps hold one connection per valve and serialise their operations).
Everything about the firmware images: none could be obtained, so the update path's behaviour on the valve side, including recovery, is unknown.

set_datetime.description: Set the valve's clock: [minute, hour, day, month, year - 2000]. Example: 2026-09-28 14:05 -> 05 0e 1c 09 1a.

format.name: day
format.notes: Day of month, 1-31.

format.name: year
format.notes: Two-digit year: raw 26 = 2026.

characteristics.name: Date and time
characteristics.notes: Five bytes, local wall-clock time, no seconds and no weekday (the valve derives the weekday, and switches summer/winter time itself per the manual). The vendor app writes the phone's local time after every successful PIN write; the schedule runs off this clock.

set_schedule_monday.description: Replace this day's schedule with up to four comfort periods. Each byte is minutes since midnight / 10 (07:30 -> 45); send 0xFF in both bytes of an unused pair. Pairs should be in ascending time order and not overlap.

format.name: period_1_start
format.notes: Minutes since midnight. 0xFF = pair unused (do not scale it).

characteristics.name: Schedule: Monday
characteristics.notes: Eight bytes: four (start, end) pairs of comfort periods, each byte minutes-since-midnight / 10 (0-144, where 144 = 24:00). 0xFF marks an unused pair. Outside the listed periods the valve holds the eco setpoint (AUTO mode). The vendor app writes 0xFF into pairs 3-4 when its "2 periods a day" option is chosen and 0x00 when "4 periods" is chosen but they are empty, and it treats only 1-143 as a real time; rikroe writes 0x00 for unused pairs and im-0 0xFF, and both treat start == end as empty. im-0 reads a pair as unused only when its END byte is above 143; a 0xFF START with a valid end it reads as "from 00:00", and it encodes a 00:00 start as 0xFF. Factory default (manual): one period, 07:00-22:00 = 2a 84 ff ff ff ff ff ff. The app's "Mon-Fri / Sat-Sun" block option just writes the same eight bytes to several days.

clear_holiday_1.description: Empty this holiday slot: 0x80 in every byte, as im-0 does. The vendor app's own empty pattern (80 01 01 ff 80 01 01 ff 0f) also works on its evidence; both rely on hour 128.

set_holiday_1.description: Program this holiday slot: from start (hour, day, month, year) to end, holding `temperature` for the whole period. Example: 2026-12-24 18:00 to 2027-01-02 12:00 at 16.5 °C -> 12 18 0c 1a 0c 02 01 1b 21.

temperature.description: °C × 2. 15 (the 7.5 °C code) = OFF, 16-56 = 8.0-28.0 °C in 0.5 °C steps, 57 (the 28.5 °C code) = ON. This is exactly the vendor app's picker; nothing outside it is documented.

format.name: start_hour
format.notes: 0-23; 128 = unset, or (rikroe) holiday already in progress.

format.name: end_hour
format.notes: 0-23; 128 or above = slot empty or expired.

characteristics.name: Holiday slot 1
characteristics.notes: Nine bytes: start (hour, day, month, year - 2000), end (hour, day, month, year - 2000), then the holiday temperature as °C × 2 (15 = OFF, 57 = ON, as in the temperature block). Whole hours only. Hour 128 (0x80) marks "no time": the vendor app treats it as unset, and rikroe reports that once a holiday is under way the valve reads back 128 in the START hour while keeping the end, and 128 or more in the end hour once the slot has expired. The vendor app's empty slot is 80 01 01 ff 80 01 01 ff 0f; im-0 clears a slot with 0x80 in every byte. The manual speaks of six vacation profiles, but the valve exposes eight slots and both apps and im-0 address all eight.

write_flags.advanced_reason: Writes the whole flags block, including bits whose meaning nobody has established; a write built from anything but a fresh read can change them silently (rikroe's mode switch clears the child lock this way). Recover by writing back the three bytes you read before the change.
write_flags.description: Write all three flag bytes. Read ee2a first and change only the bit you mean: child lock = byte 0 | 0x80 (on) or & 0x7F (off); manual mode = byte 0 | 0x01, auto = byte 0 & 0xFE. Bytes 1 and 2 go back exactly as read.

flags_0.description: Byte 0 as read, with bit 7 (child lock) and/or bit 0 (manual mode) changed.

format.name: manual_mode
format.notes: rikroe's reading (hardware-tested on a Sygonix HT100 BT); the vendor app never touches it.

format.name: child_lock
format.notes: The vendor app's child-lock switch. The same lock the valve sets when OK and the timer key are held for about 2 s (manual).

format.name: flags_0
format.notes: The whole first byte, for read-modify-write.

format.name: flags_1
format.notes: Meaning unknown; write back what was read.

format.name: flags_2
format.notes: Meaning unknown; write back what was read.

characteristics.name: Flags
characteristics.notes: Three bytes of flags. Byte 0 bit 7 (0x80) is the child lock — the only bit the vendor app writes: it reads the three bytes, sets or clears bit 7 and writes all three back unchanged otherwise. rikroe reads byte 0 bit 0 (0x01) as manual (MANU) mode and switches modes by writing byte 0 = 0x01 or 0x00 with 0x80 in bytes 1-2 — which also clears the child lock and any other bit, so read first. What the remaining bits of byte 0 and bytes 1-2 mean is not known; im-0 only prints them in binary. Unlike the temperature block, 0x80 is NOT a safe "unchanged" filler for byte 0: it is the child-lock bit.

comfort.description: °C × 2. 15 (the 7.5 °C code) = OFF, 16-56 = 8.0-28.0 °C in 0.5 °C steps, 57 (the 28.5 °C code) = ON. This is exactly the vendor app's picker; nothing outside it is documented.

eco.description: °C × 2. 15 (the 7.5 °C code) = OFF, 16-56 = 8.0-28.0 °C in 0.5 °C steps, 57 (the 28.5 °C code) = ON. This is exactly the vendor app's picker; nothing outside it is documented.

set_manual_temperature.description: Set the active setpoint (the same as turning the wheel): 80 <setpoint> 80 80 80 80 80. In AUTO the valve returns to the schedule at the next switch point. OFF (15) closes the valve, ON (57) opens it fully. EUROprog 2 never changes this byte (it writes back what it read); this is how im-0 and Home Assistant set the target. The range is the one the valve's own wheel and the vendor app's comfort/eco pickers allow, nothing wider.

setpoint.description: °C × 2. 15 (the 7.5 °C code) = OFF, 16-56 = 8.0-28.0 °C in 0.5 °C steps, 57 (the 28.5 °C code) = ON. This is exactly the vendor app's picker; nothing outside it is documented.

set_temperature_offset.description: Set the sensor calibration offset: 80 80 80 80 <offset> 80 80, offset as signed °C × 2. Example: -1.5 °C -> raw -3 -> fd.

offset.description: -5.0..+5.0 °C in 0.5 °C steps, the vendor app's range.

set_window_open_minutes.description: Set how long the valve stays closed after an open window: 80 80 80 80 80 80 <minutes>.

format.name: current_temp
format.notes: Measured at the valve head. im-0 reads it signed; the vendor app unsigned (identical for 0-63.5 °C). Always write 0x80 here.

format.name: manual_temp
format.notes: The setpoint the valve is regulating to right now (rikroe's and Home Assistant's reading): in AUTO it follows comfort/eco per the schedule, and a write overrides it until the next switch point, like turning the wheel. 15 = OFF, 57 = ON. im-0 names it the manual-mode temperature.

format.name: eco_temp
format.notes: Eco (energy-saving) setpoint, used outside schedule periods. im-0's target_temp_l. Factory 16 °C (32).

format.name: comfort_temp
format.notes: Comfort setpoint, used inside schedule periods. im-0's target_temp_h. Factory 21 °C (42).

format.name: temp_offset
format.notes: Calibration offset, signed, -10..10 = -5.0..+5.0 °C. 0x80 (-128) = unset.

format.name: window_open_sensitivity
format.notes: The codes the vendor app writes. The manual gives medium as the factory setting, yet im-0's example unit reads 4; rikroe treats 0xF0 here as "window open", which may be a state flag. Only 4, 8 and 12 are documented as writable.

format.name: window_open_minutes
format.notes: How long the valve stays closed after detecting an open window: 10-60 in steps of 10 in the vendor app. Factory 10.

characteristics.name: Temperatures
characteristics.notes: Seven bytes, temperatures as °C × 2. In every byte a client is not changing, send 0x80: im-0 and rikroe both use it as "leave this field as it is", and it is also the vendor app's value for an unset field. The vendor app instead reads the block, edits its own fields and writes all seven back — including a stale copy of the measured temperature in byte 0, which the valve evidently ignores. Setpoint codes: 15 (7.5 °C) = OFF, which closes the valve (frost protection stays active per the manual); 57 (28.5 °C) = ON, valve fully open; 16-56 = 8.0-28.0 °C. The vendor app offers exactly OFF, 8.0-28.0 and ON for comfort and eco, -5.0..+5.0 °C for the offset, low / medium / high window sensitivity and 10-60 minutes.

characteristics.name: Battery
characteristics.notes: One byte, percent. 0xFF (-1 signed) = not measured yet; the vendor app re-reads after 1 s while it sees that. Home Assistant's documentation warns the reading "may not be very accurate". The vendor app's parser accepts only -1..99, so it silently ignores a reading of exactly 100 and keeps showing the previous value.

characteristics.name: Second revision string
characteristics.notes: A string im-0 labels "firmware revision #2" (PIN required to read); rikroe lists it as unknown. The vendor apps never touch it.

characteristics.name: LCD timer (per im-0)
characteristics.notes: Two bytes the vendor app reads and ignores. im-0 decodes them as an LCD timer (preload, current) and writes [preload, 0x00]; what the preload value controls, and its unit, are not established, so no command is declared.

authenticate.description: Present the PIN, uint32 little-endian. Must be the first write of every connection. PIN 0 -> 00 00 00 00; PIN 123456 -> 40 e2 01 00 (rikroe's test vectors).

pin.description: The valve's access PIN, 0-999999. Factory default 0 (the manual's "000 000"). If the owner changed it in EUROprog 2, or set a room PIN in ET Blue (which never uses 0), it is the number they chose there; it is not printed on the unit.

change_pin.advanced_reason: Replaces the secret every later connection must present. A mistyped or forgotten PIN locks every client out; the only recourse is the valve's menu reset, and whether that restores PIN 0 is not established. Write the new value down before sending it.
change_pin.description: Set a new PIN, uint32 little-endian, in a connection already authenticated with the current one. Every other client must then be given the new value.

new_pin.description: The new PIN, at most six decimal digits (the vendor app's limit).

characteristics.name: PIN
characteristics.notes: The access gate. The first successful write in a connection authenticates it; a further write while authenticated sets a new PIN (the vendor app's "change PIN" and im-0's `set pin` both work this way). Use write requests: the write status is the verdict. Whether a wrong PIN produces an ATT error, a disconnect or both is not established.

characteristics.name: Firmware update channel
characteristics.notes: The vendor app's firmware-update channel (features[firmware_update]; protocol_details.firmware_update). Twenty-byte writes carry an image; twenty-byte-or-shorter notifications carry the valve's flow control. Described at role level only. A generic client must never write here: the image is unsigned and an interrupted or malformed transfer may leave the valve unusable.

initialization.description: Write the owner's PIN to 47e9ee30-47e9-11e4-8939-164230d1df67 as a uint32 little-endian — the characteristic's `authenticate` command, whose `pin` parameter is the stored credential — using a write request, before any other read or write on this service. Write status 0 means accepted; any other status means a wrong PIN. The factory PIN 0 is the four bytes 00 00 00 00. Documented rather than executable because the value is per unit.
initialization.notes: On firmware whose revision string sorts below the vendor app's reference revision the app waits 1 s before this write; waiting 1 s on every connect is harmless. The vendor app then writes the current date and time (ee01) once per session.

services.name: Comet Blue thermostat service
services.notes: Every setting is a fixed-length value on its own characteristic; there is no command channel, framing or checksum. Read and write with plain GATT reads and write requests. All writes, and (per im-0) the reads of everything below except ee30, need a successful PIN write earlier in the same connection. The handle layout has never been dumped; clients should match characteristics by UUID (im-0 and the vendor app both do). Characteristic properties below are inferred from what the vendor app and the open implementations do with each value, not read from a GATT dump. rikroe's library documents that the valve applies written values when the connection closes rather than on each write, so a client should disconnect after writing and not trust a read-back taken in the same connection.

characteristics.name: Model Number String
characteristics.notes: "Comet Blue" (im-0 matches it case-insensitively).

characteristics.name: Firmware Revision String
characteristics.notes: Controller firmware revision: four letters and four digits on im-0's example unit. The vendor app compares it as a string against a reference revision to decide whether to delay the PIN write, and against the downloadable image to decide whether to offer an update.

characteristics.name: Software Revision String
characteristics.notes: Radio-module software revision. On im-0's example unit it is a dotted version with a Sygonix suffix, so it may be the easiest way to tell a rebadge apart after connecting (unconfirmed).

characteristics.name: Manufacturer Name String
characteristics.notes: "eurotronic gmbh" when lower-cased (im-0's discovery check).

services.name: Device Information
services.notes: Standard Device Information strings, readable without the PIN (the vendor app exempts the firmware and software revision strings from its PIN gate, and im-0 reads all four before authenticating). The parent service is assumed to be the standard Device Information service (0000180a-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb); both the vendor app and im-0 find these characteristics by UUID alone. The GAP device name (00002a00-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb) reads "Comet Blue" on im-0's example unit.
